prospect.name: Andy
prospect.location: New Zealand (small town); originally from the USA
prospect.occupation: Self-employed event director — runs his own adventure race; recently took a new job
prospect.family_status: Going through a separation after a 25-year marriage; two sons, one 17 and at university studying sports science; has a twin brother
prospect.training_background: Lifelong endurance and outdoor athlete — expedition climbing, surfing, paddling, Ironman-distance racing, now expedition-level adventure racing. Currently 1-2 kettlebell days, 2 lifting days, 3 cycling days and climbing 3-4 nights a week. Wrote a book on high-intensity interval training for endurance; physics degree.
prospect.medical: Bilateral hip replacements — first about 4-5 years ago, second roughly 18 months later, clear of surgery about 2-2.5 years. Underlying congenital hip condition. States the prosthetic socket 'has changed... I don't have as much surface and it can pop out more easily'. Also arthritic shoulders and sore elbows under heavy load, and four weeks of physio for his back after returning to deadlifts.

signals: Already very fit at 50 — 12% body fat, climbs 3-4x/week, races at expedition level; says outright 'there's nothing wrong right now'
Wants skill progression and safe loading rather than rescue: 'part of it is wanting to be able to progress without hurting myself'
Rep framed him as above the usual client: 'you're not our typical client because you're way ahead'
Deviates from a pure optimizer on price — treated the fee as 'a substantial portion of my annual income', so price was a genuine barrier rather than a quality signal

goals.text: Learn to progress with kettlebells safely and choose correct loads instead of self-programming badly
Improve mobility, which he names as his one weakness, around two hip replacements
Train anywhere — take a couple of kettlebells in the van on surf and road trips and keep consistency without a gym
Keep enough muscle and capability to climb, surf and race rather than be 'a cyclist that doesn't have any muscle'
Reconnect with who he was and what he likes doing after the separation
Possibly build a side business coaching kettlebells in his small town

pains.text: Joints suffer under traditional lifting — arthritic shoulders, sore elbows on weighted pull-ups, four weeks of physio for his back after returning to deadlifts
Two hip replacements limit some movements; the artificial socket 'can pop out more easily'
Does not know enough about kettlebell progression — picks weights that are too heavy on complexes and is wrecked the next day
Too much kettlebell content online to sift; would burn a lot of time building and optimising his own program
Schedules work commitments around gym days, which he calls silly, and loses training when travelling
Two separate households after the separation have left him financially stretched

objections.raw_quote: So I will, let me think, and I can have some time to think about that, right?
objections.rep_response: Accepted it immediately — 'Let me know what are your thoughts' — and moved to booking a callback.

objections.raw_quote: Well, I have to figure out if I can run it through my business, for one. That's my first step.
objections.rep_response: Asked what he meant, let him explain the New Zealand tax treatment, then asked for a timeline on the accountant's answer.

objections.raw_quote: There is a financial concern for me at the moment. I'm very time-free and my kids are out the house, which is good, but that is a significant, that would be a significant investment for me.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it — asked whether anything besides finances was in the way — then went straight to booking Friday. No payment plan offered and no financial picture taken.

objections.raw_quote: that's really looking at about 7,500 New Zealand dollars for me because of the exchange rate... that's a substantial portion of my annual income, so I just have to think about that
objections.rep_response: No rebuttal or reframe; acknowledged and scheduled the follow-up.

prospect_financials.note: No financial picture was taken. Prospect volunteered only that $4,000 USD is about NZ$7,500 and 'a substantial portion of my annual income', and that expensing it through his business would net it to roughly $2,800 USD.

evidence: Prospect asked for time: 'let me think, and I can have some time to think about that, right?'
Two blockers left open — accountant confirmation on expensing it, and whether he can afford it at all
Rep booked a specific callback: '6.30pm, Friday, 29... I will set up a meeting and you'll get the invite through your email'

Counter-evidence that this is warmer than a cold follow-up: 'apart from the finances, the three months of, yeah, three months is good. Everything else, the way that it works and what I think I would get out of it are good.'
No payment taken, no payment link sent, no verbal agreement to proceed
outcome.next_step: Callback Friday the 29th at 18:30 New Zealand time, after he asks his accountant whether the program can be expensed through his business.

notable.note: Rep quoted an off-menu three-month tier at $4,000 USD and actively steered the prospect off the standard packages — 'Most of the guys go for the 12-month and six-month, but that's not for you, in my opinion'. Separately, the prospect has two hip replacements and arthritic shoulders and was pitched loaded ballistic kettlebell work with no clinician clearance sought; the rep also asserted that joint damage is 'impossible' with kettlebells.

quality.notes: Labels invert repeatedly and for long stretches. The whole hip-surgery exchange around 00:09:00 is reversed — the rep is the one who says he needs the surgery and the prospect is the one advising him — and the entire pillar presentation from roughly 00:35:30 to 00:39:30 is attributed to the prospect. The rep is labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the Drive folder is 'Andrew Musial'; treated as the same rep. The prospect's surname is never stated.
